subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should this TUI scroll-jump tracker be fixed primarily in pi-tui, in OpenClaw's TUI viewport/follow state, or by adding an explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the durable fix changes terminal rendering behavior and may depend on third-party renderer ownership versus OpenClaw product UX policy.

options.title: Patch renderer first
options.body: Fix or patch the pi-tui content-driven full-redraw path, then add OpenClaw viewport anchoring only if live PTY proof still shows jumps.

options.title: Own TUI follow policy
options.body: Implement an OpenClaw TUI anchor/follow state around ChatLog updates and history refreshes, accepting that it may still need renderer coordination for scrollback clearing.

options.title: Add a TUI preference
options.body: Add an explicit user-facing TUI auto-scroll mode only after deciding that configurable behavior is preferable to a stable default.

recommendation.title: Patch renderer first
recommendation.body: Fix or patch the pi-tui content-driven full-redraw path, then add OpenClaw viewport anchoring only if live PTY proof still shows jumps.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans TUI product behavior and pi-tui/dependency integration, where the history points to steipete as the broadest routing owner.
